title: Vault audit, policy and secret access
volume: None on a normal day for audit devices. Policies change with releases, a few a week where Terraform runs them. Denied reads come with misconfigured apps, so expect some until those are fixed.
mdr_note: These detections are yours to work. Sophos MDR doesn't work custom detections, and a case your own case rule opens from them is Managed By Self.
author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: Three custom detection rules for HashiCorp Vault, on the CloudAudit records the library's Vault parsers write from Vault's audit device. They make a detection when someone disables an audit device, writes or deletes an ACL policy, or is denied a secret read. Each rule matches sensor type HashiCorp Vault only.
notes:
Setup:
- Add the library's Vault parsers, and turn on a Vault audit device and forward its lines to the data collector, as the parser entry says. Then run the check-your-data search to see events arrive.

How it works:
- The parsers write each API call's operation (read, list, create, update, delete) as the event name and its path as object_key, from the response entry Vault logs for the call.
- The audit rule takes a delete on a path under sys/audit/, the call that disables an audit device. The policy rule takes writes and deletes under sys/policies/acl/ and the older sys/policy/.
- The denied read rule takes reads and lists that Vault answered with permission denied.

Tuning:
- If an automation account writes policies on every deploy, leave it out of the policy rule in the query itself, such as and user_name != 'approle-terraform'. A suppression rule would hide Sophos's detections for that account as well.

Testing:
- In a lab tenant on 2026-11-23, each query returned exactly the sample lines tests.json lists in Data Lake Search, and the rules run offline on the same 5 records agreed. The samples went in with their dates moved to the day before the test, so they fell inside the search's time range.
- As live rules there, each one fired on exactly its sample lines within about a minute. The lines went in 17 minutes after the rules were made, and every rule fired on the first send.
- No Sophos detector made a detection on the lines these rules take. Sophos's sign-in analytics flagged only sample sign-ins on Auth, as an unseen user, address or application.
- The lines went to HTTP Ingest one per request as text, the way a syslog line arrives.

Known gaps:
- Disabling the only audit device leaves nothing to record what follows. Run two, so removing one is still recorded by the other.
- Vault hashes most values with HMAC, so the detection names the Vault identity and the path, not the token.
